sanskrit: tac chrutvā rājaśārdūla viśvāmitrasya bhāṣitam muhūrtam iva niḥsaṃjñaḥ saṃjñāvān idam abravīt
english: Hearing that speech of Viśvāmitra, O tiger among kings, he was as though unconscious for a moment; then, regaining his senses, he spoke thus:

sanskrit: ūnaṣoḍaśavarṣo me rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ na yuddhayogyatām asya paśyāmi saha rākṣasaiḥ
english: My lotus-eyed Rāma is not yet sixteen years old; I do not see him fit for battle against the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: iyam akṣauhiṇī pūrṇā yasyāhaṃ patir īśvaraḥ anayā saṃvṛto gatvā yodhāhaṃ tair niśācaraiḥ
english: A full akṣauhiṇī army of which I am the master and lord — covered by this force I shall go and fight those night-roaming demons myself.

sanskrit: ime śūrāś ca vikrāntā bhṛtyā me 'straviśāradāḥ yogyā rakṣogaṇair yoddhuṃ na rāmaṃ netum arhasi
english: These valiant and mighty retainers of mine are skilled in arms and capable of fighting the hosts of rākṣasas. You ought not to take Rāma.

sanskrit: aham eva dhanuṣpāṇir goptā samaramūrdhani yāvat prāṇān dhariṣyāmi tāvad yotsye niśācaraiḥ
english: I myself, bow in hand, shall be the protector in the forefront of battle; as long as I hold life within me, I shall fight those night-roamers.

sanskrit: nirvighnā vratacaryā sā bhaviṣyati surakṣitā ahaṃ tatra gamiṣyāmi na rāma netum arhasi
english: That observance of the vow shall be unimpeded and well protected; I shall go there myself. You ought not to take Rāma.

sanskrit: bālo hy akṛtavidyaś ca na ca vetti balābalam na cāstrabalasaṃyukto na ca yuddhaviśāradaḥ na cāsau rakṣasāṃ yogyaḥ kūṭayuddhā hi te dhruvam
english: He is still a boy, his learning incomplete; he does not know strength from weakness, he is not furnished with the power of weapons, and he is not skilled in warfare. Nor is he a match for the rākṣasas — for they fight with treachery, that is certain.

sanskrit: viprayukto hi rāmeṇa muhūrtam api notsahe jīvituṃ muniśārdūla na rāmaṃ netum arhasi
english: Separated from Rāma I could not endure to live even for a moment, O tiger among sages. You ought not to take Rāma.

sanskrit: yadi vā rāghavaṃ brahman netum icchasi suvrata caturaṅgasamāyuktaṃ mayā saha ca taṃ naya
english: Or if, O brāhmaṇa, O steadfast in vows, you desire to take the Rāghava, then take him together with me, equipped with a four-divisioned army.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭir varṣasahasrāṇi jātasya mama kauśika duḥkhenotpāditaś cāyaṃ na rāmaṃ netum arhasi
english: Sixty thousand years have passed since my birth, O Kauśika, and he was obtained by me through great hardship and pain. You ought not to take Rāma.

sanskrit: caturṇām ātmajānāṃ hi prītiḥ paramikā mama jyeṣṭhaṃ dharmapradhānaṃ ca na rāmaṃ netum arhasi
english: My delight in all four of my sons is supreme, and Rāma — the eldest, foremost in righteousness — is especially dear. You ought not to take Rāma.

sanskrit: kiṃ vīryā rākṣasās te ca kasya putrāś ca ke ca te kathaṃ pramāṇāḥ ke caitān rakṣanti munipuṃgava
english: What is the prowess of those rākṣasas? Whose sons are they, and who are they? What is their stature? Who guards them, O foremost among sages?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca pratikartavyaṃ teṣāṃ rāmeṇa rakṣasām māmakair vā balair brahman mayā vā kūṭayodhinām
english: And how are those rākṣasas, those treacherous fighters, to be countered — by Rāma, or by my forces, O brāhmaṇa, or by me?

sanskrit: sarvaṃ me śaṃsa bhagavan kathaṃ teṣāṃ mayā raṇe sthātavyaṃ duṣṭabhāvānāṃ vīryotsiktā hi rākṣasāḥ
english: Tell me everything, O blessed one — how I am to stand against those evil-natured ones in battle, for the rākṣasas are inflated with their own might.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā viśvāmitro 'bhyabhāṣata paulastyavaṃśaprabhavo rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ
english: Hearing his words, Viśvāmitra replied: There is a rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa, born of the lineage of Paulastya —

sanskrit: sa brahmaṇā dattavaras trailokyaṃ bādhate bhṛśam mahābalo mahāvīryo rākṣasair bahubhir vṛtaḥ
english: — he is endowed with a boon granted by Brahmā, and he greatly oppresses all three worlds; of immense strength and immense valour, he is surrounded by many rākṣasas.

sanskrit: śrūyate hi mahāvīryo rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ sākṣād vaiśravaṇabhrātā putro viśravaso muneḥ
english: It is heard that the great-valoured Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, is the very brother of Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera), the son of the sage Viśravas.

sanskrit: yadā svayaṃ na yajñasya vighnakartā mahābalaḥ tena saṃcoditau tau tu rākṣasau sumahā balau mārīcaś ca subāhuś ca yajñavighnaṃ kariṣyataḥ
english: When the great-powerful one does not himself create obstruction to the sacrifice, he sends forth two rākṣasas of exceedingly great strength — Mārīca and Subāhu — who will cause the disruption of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: ity ukto muninā tena rājovāca muniṃ tadā na hi śakto 'smi saṃgrāme sthātuṃ tasya durātmanaḥ
english: Thus addressed by that sage, the king then spoke to the sage: I am truly not capable of standing in battle against that wicked-souled one.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ prasādaṃ dharmajña kuruṣva mama putrake devadānavagandharvā yakṣāḥ pataga pannagāḥ
english: Therefore show grace to my boy, O knower of dharma — gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, birds, and serpents —

sanskrit: na śaktā rāvaṇaṃ soḍhuṃ kiṃ punar mānavā yudhi sa hi vīryavatāṃ vīryam ādatte yudhi rākṣasaḥ
english: — are not able to withstand Rāvaṇa; how much less then could mortals in battle? For that rākṣasa in combat seizes away the very valour of the valiant.

sanskrit: tena cāhaṃ na śakto 'smi saṃyoddhuṃ tasya vā balaiḥ sabalo vā muniśreṣṭha sahito vā mamātmajaiḥ
english: Against him I am not capable of fighting — neither with his forces, O foremost of sages, nor with my own forces together with my sons at my side.

sanskrit: katham apy amaraprakhyaṃ saṃgrāmāṇām akovidam bālaṃ me tanayaṃ brahman naiva dāsyāmi putrakam
english: How could I in any way give you my boy — a child, godlike in appearance, but inexperienced in battles, O brāhmaṇa, my little son?

sanskrit: atha kālopamau yuddhe sutau sundopasundayoḥ yajñavighnakarau tau te naiva dāsyāmi putrakam
english: Moreover, those two sons of Sunda and Upasunda who are like Death itself in battle and who are the disruptors of your sacrifice — I will surely not give you my boy for them.

sanskrit: mārīcaś ca subāhuś ca vīryavantau suśikṣitau tayor anyatareṇāhaṃ yoddhā syāṃ sasuhṛdgaṇaḥ
english: Mārīca and Subāhu are both mighty and well-trained; against either one of the two, I might fight along with my band of allies.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya snehaparyākulākṣaram samanyuḥ kauśiko vākyaṃ pratyuvaca mahīpatim
english: Hearing his speech, which was confused with affection at every syllable, Kauśika, filled with anger, replied to the king of the earth:

sanskrit: pūrvam arthaṃ pratiśrutya pratijñāṃ hātum icchasi rāgavāṇām ayukto 'yaṃ kulasyāsya viparyayaḥ
english: Having first promised the thing, you now wish to abandon your pledge. This reversal is unworthy of and ill-befitting this lineage of the Rāghus.

sanskrit: yad idaṃ te kṣamaṃ rājan gamiṣyāmi yathāgatam mithyāpratijñaḥ kākutstha sukhī bhava sabāndhavaḥ
english: If this be fitting for you, O king, I shall depart as I came. O Kākutstha, false to your promise — be happy with your kinsmen!

sanskrit: tasya roṣaparītasya viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ cacāla vasudhā kṛtsnā viveśa ca bhayaṃ surān
english: As the wise Viśvāmitra was overcome by wrath, the entire earth trembled, and fear entered into the gods.

sanskrit: trastarūpaṃ tu vijñāya jagat sarvaṃ mahān ṛṣiḥ nṛpatiṃ suvrato dhīro vasiṣṭho vākyam abravīt
english: Perceiving that all the world had assumed the form of fear, the great sage, steadfast in vows, the wise Vasiṣṭha, spoke these words to the king:

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇāṃ kule jātaḥ sākṣād dharma ivāparaḥ dhṛtimānsuvrataḥ śrīmān na dharmaṃ hātum arhasi
english: Born in the lineage of the Ikṣvākus, like dharma himself made manifest, endowed with steadfastness, virtuous in vows, resplendent — you ought not to abandon dharma.

sanskrit: triṣu lokeṣu vikhyāto dharmātmā iti rāghavaḥ svadharmaṃ pratipadyasva nādharmaṃ voḍhum arhasi
english: The Rāghava is renowned in the three worlds as one whose soul is dharma. Follow your own dharma; you ought not to bear adharma.

sanskrit: saṃśrutyaivaṃ kariṣyāmīty akurvāṇasya rāghava iṣṭāpūrtavadho bhūyāt tasmād rāmaṃ visarjaya
english: For one who has pledged 'I will do this' and then fails to do it, O Rāghava, the fruits of his ritual offerings and charitable works are destroyed. Therefore release Rāma.

sanskrit: kṛtāstram akṛtāstraṃ vā nainaṃ śakṣyanti rākṣasāḥ guptaṃ kuśikaputreṇa jvalanenāmṛtaṃ yathā
english: Whether trained in arms or not yet trained, the rākṣasas will not be able to overpower him — guarded as he will be by the son of Kuśika, as ambrosia is guarded by fire.

sanskrit: eṣa vigrahavān dharma eṣa vīryavatāṃ varaḥ eṣa buddhyādhiko loke tapasaś ca parāyaṇam
english: He (Viśvāmitra) is dharma embodied in bodily form; he is the best among the mighty; he is supreme in intellect in this world and the ultimate resort of tapas.

sanskrit: eṣo 'strān vividhān vetti trailokye sacarācare nainam anyaḥ pumān vetti na ca vetsyanti ke cana
english: He knows diverse weapons in all the three worlds, movable and immovable; no other man knows him fully, nor shall any ever know him.

sanskrit: na devā narṣayaḥ ke cin nāsurā na ca rākṣasāḥ gandharvayakṣapravarāḥ sakiṃnaramahoragāḥ
english: Neither the gods, nor any sages, nor the asuras, nor the rākṣasas, nor the foremost gandharvas and yakṣas, nor kiṃnaras, nor great serpents —

sanskrit: sarvāstrāṇi kṛśāśvasya putrāḥ paramadhārmikāḥ kauśikāya purā dattā yadā rājyaṃ praśāsati
english: — the all-righteous sons of Kṛśāśva gave all their weapons in former times to Kauśika (Viśvāmitra) when he was ruling as king.

sanskrit: te 'pi putrāḥ kṛśāśvasya prajāpatisutāsutāḥ naikarūpā mahāvīryā dīptimanto jayāvahāḥ
english: Those sons of Kṛśāśva too, being the grandsons of Prajāpati's daughters, are of many forms, of great valour, radiant, and bringers of victory.

sanskrit: jayā ca suprabhā caiva dakṣakanye sumadhyame te suvāte 'straśastrāṇi śataṃ parama bhāsvaram
english: Jayā and Suprabhā, the two slender-waisted daughters of Dakṣa — they gave birth to one hundred supremely radiant weapons and missiles.

sanskrit: pañcāśataṃ sutāṃl lebhe jayā nāma varān purā vadhāyāsurasainyānām ameyān kāmarūpiṇaḥ
english: Jayā in former times obtained fifty excellent sons, immeasurable and able to assume any form at will, for the slaying of the armies of the asuras.

sanskrit: suprabhājanayac cāpi putrān pañcāśataṃ punaḥ saṃhārān nāma durdharṣān durākrāmān balīyasaḥ
english: And Suprabhā in turn gave birth to fifty sons named the Saṃhāras — irresistible, impossible to assail, and most powerful.

sanskrit: tāni cāstrāṇi vetty eṣa yathāvat kuśikātmajaḥ apūrvāṇāṃ ca janane śakto bhūyaś ca dharmavit
english: And the son of Kuśika knows all those weapons rightly and fully; moreover he is capable of creating weapons never known before, being also learned in dharma.

sanskrit: evaṃ vīryo mahātejā viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ na rāmagamane rājan saṃśayaṃ gantum arhasi
english: Such is the valour and great energy of the great ascetic Viśvāmitra. O king, you ought not to entertain doubt about Rāma's going.

sanskrit: tathā vasiṣṭhe bruvati rājā daśarathaḥ sutam prahṛṣṭavadano rāmam ājuhāva salakṣmaṇam
english: While Vasiṣṭha spoke thus, king Daśaratha, with joyful countenance, summoned his son Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: kṛtasvastyayanaṃ mātrā pitrā daśarathena ca purodhasā vasiṣṭhena maṅgalair abhimantritam
english: Having had the auspicious rite of blessing performed — by his mother, by his father Daśaratha, and by the family priest Vasiṣṭha who consecrated him with benedictions —

sanskrit: sa putraṃ mūrdhny upāghrāya rājā daśarathaḥ priyam dadau kuśikaputrāya suprītenāntarātmanā
english: — king Daśaratha smelled his beloved son's head and, with his inner soul well pleased, entrusted him to the son of Kuśika.

sanskrit: tato vāyuḥ sukhasparśo virajasko vavau tadā viśvāmitragataṃ rāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājīvalocanam
english: Then a wind, pleasant to the touch and free of dust, blew upon seeing the lotus-eyed Rāma depart with Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: puṣpavṛṣṭir mahaty āsīd devadundubhinisvanaḥ śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣaḥ prayāte tu mahātmani
english: As the great-souled one set forth, there was a great shower of flowers, the sound of the divine kettledrum, and the reverberation of conch shells and drums.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro yayāv agre tato rāmo mahāyaśāḥ kākapakṣadharo dhanvī taṃ ca saumitrir anvagāt
english: Viśvāmitra went ahead; behind him followed the greatly renowned Rāma, bearing the kākapakṣa locks of youth, bow in hand; and Saumitri (Lakṣmaṇa) followed him in turn.

sanskrit: kalāpinau dhanuṣpāṇī śobhayānau diśo daśa viśvāmitraṃ mahātmānaṃ triśīrṣāv iva pannagau anujagmatur akṣudrau pitāmaham ivāśvinau
english: Adorned with quivers, bows in hand, illuminating all ten directions, the two noble princes followed the great-souled Viśvāmitra like two three-headed serpents, like the two Aśvins attending Brahmā.

sanskrit: baddhagodhāṅgulitrāṇau khaḍgavantau mahādyutī sthāṇuṃ devam ivācintyaṃ kumārāv iva pāvakī
english: With finger-guards and leather wristbands fastened, bearing swords, blazing with great splendour, the two princes were like the twin sons of Agni attending the unthinkable, immovable divine post.

sanskrit: adhyardhayojanaṃ gatvā sarayvā dakṣiṇe taṭe rāmeti madhurā vāṇīṃ viśvāmitro 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Having gone one and a half yojanas to the southern bank of the Sarayū, Viśvāmitra addressed Rāma in a sweet voice: 'Rāma —'

sanskrit: gṛhāṇa vatsa salilaṃ mā bhūt kālasya paryayaḥ mantragrāmaṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ balām atibalāṃ tathā
english: 'Receive water, dear child, lest the moment pass. Receive the group of mantras — receive both Balā and Atibalā.'

sanskrit: na śramo na jvaro vā te na rūpasya viparyayaḥ na ca suptaṃ pramattaṃ vā dharṣayiṣyanti nairṛtāḥ
english: 'Neither fatigue, nor fever, nor any change in your form shall afflict you; and the rākṣasas shall not be able to strike you down when asleep or when off-guard.'

sanskrit: na bāhvoḥ sadṛśo vīrye pṛthivyām asti kaś cana triṣu lokeṣu vā rāma na bhavet sadṛśas tava
english: 'There is none equal to you in the valour of your arms on this earth, O Rāma, nor in the three worlds could any equal be found.'

sanskrit: na saubhāgye na dākṣiṇye na jñāne buddhiniścaye nottare pratipattavyo samo loke tavānagha
english: 'In beauty, in grace, in knowledge, in the resolve of intellect, and in apt reply, no equal to you is to be found in this world, O sinless one.'

sanskrit: etadvidyādvaye labdhe bhavitā nāsti te samaḥ balā cātibalā caiva sarvajñānasya mātarau
english: 'When you have acquired these two sciences, there will be none equal to you; for Balā and Atibalā are the mothers of all knowledge.'

sanskrit: kṣutpipāse na te rāma bhaviṣyete narottama balām atibalāṃ caiva paṭhataḥ pathi rāghava vidyādvayam adhīyāne yaśaś cāpy atulaṃ bhuvi
english: 'Hunger and thirst shall not afflict you, O best of men; O Rāghava, as you recite on the path Balā and Atibalā — studying these two sciences — matchless renown on earth shall also be yours.'

sanskrit: pitāmahasute hy ete vidye tejaḥsamanvite pradātuṃ tava kākutstha sadṛśas tvaṃ hi dhārmika
english: 'These two sciences, born of the granddaughters of Brahmā and endowed with brilliance, are fit to be bestowed upon you alone, O Kākutstha — for you are righteous and a worthy recipient.'

sanskrit: kāmaṃ bahuguṇāḥ sarve tvayy ete nātra saṃśayaḥ tapasā saṃbhṛte caite bahurūpe bhaviṣyataḥ
english: 'Indeed, all these many virtues are in you — of that there is no doubt; and sustained by tapas, these sciences will manifest in many forms for you.'

sanskrit: tato rāmo jalaṃ spṛṣṭvā prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ śuciḥ pratijagrāha te vidye maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ vidyāsamudito rāmaḥ śuśubhe bhūrivikramaḥ
english: Then Rāma, with joyful countenance, having touched water and become ritually pure, received those two sciences from the great sage of purified soul; gladdened by the sciences, Rāma of boundless valour shone resplendent.

sanskrit: gurukāryāṇi sarvāṇi niyujya kuśikātmaje ūṣus tāṃ rajanīṃ tatra sarayvāṃ susukhaṃ trayaḥ
english: Having entrusted all the duties of the teacher to the son of Kuśika, the three of them spent that night there on the banks of the Sarayū in great comfort.
